start.text: Twenty thousand years ago, somewhere in Ice Age Europe, it starts to rain.

week.text: Not a shower. A whole week of it.

what.text: No weather app. No hardware store. Just twenty people, and whatever they had on their backs. So what do you do?

left.text: Nobody wrote it down. But they left a lot behind: hearths, tools, bones, even paintings. And a few hunter-gatherers alive today help us read it.

dayOne.text: Day one. First job: get out of the wet. Wet clothes steal body heat, and in the Ice Age that could kill you.

huts.text: A cave, if you were lucky. If not, a hut: a frame of branches, or even mammoth bones, covered in hides. In what is now Ukraine, people built exactly that.
